This is the story of my first psychedelic experience. This happened quite a few years ago, so it's all a bit fuzzy, and I'm sure there are many parts of the trip that I have completely forgotten. I'll do my best to attempt to recreate the events of that day.

I was a senior in high school, and though I'd been smoking cannabis for the past 5 years, it was the only "psychedelic" drug that I had ever tried. A friend told me that he was getting psilocybin mushrooms, so I eagerly got him to pick me up a quarter ounce of them. I always researched drugs thoroughly before trying them, so I decided a starter dose of 2 grams was the way to go.

The day I took them was a beautiful spring day; the sun was shining, the leaves were almost fully back, and it was warm enough that I was wearing shorts and a t-shirt. I rode my bicycle to a friend's house to use his scale, and took just over 2 grams of mushrooms. I spent roughly half an hour waiting for the mushrooms to kick in, before foolishly deciding to take another 2 grams, thinking they were just weak mushrooms. Despite having researched it, and knowing that if I waited another half hour they would likely have kicked in, I ended up taking 4 grams of mushrooms in less than an hour.

Shortly after taking my second dose of psilocybin mushrooms, I got a call from another friend inviting me to come hangout at his house. This friend's house was always loud, busy, and full of stoners. Not the best place to be during a mushroom trip. I decided to go however, and started off on a bike ride all the way from the south to the north end of my town. Normally, this would take 15-20 minutes maximum, but this day it took me roughly 45 minutes.

I remember biking full speed down the sidewalk, with bushes on one side and trees overhead, and thinking that I was in a tunnel of nature. It was incredibly beautiful, and even though the sidewalk seemed to keep extending in front of me the further I rode, I didn't care if I was trapped. I was enjoying myself so much, I didn't notice a car backing out of it's driveway until it was almost too late. I recall veering off onto the road sharply, and feeling a wave of paranoia. I'm not sure if I thought the person in the car was a police officer, or that they'd call the police, or even if I just thought that they were mad at me. All I really remember about that was just negative emotions, which spurred me to escape.

I turned off the route to my friend's house, and went to a nearby nature trail/forested area. I took a few minutes to catch my breath, and just walked around and took in the nature. This is by far my fondest memory from this trip; nature just felt like where I was supposed to be.

Eventually, I arrived at my friend's house, which was full of loud stoners, and a few strangers. At first, I thought I was okay there; I remember staring at the hardwood floors, which seemed to be almost floating and moving back and forth. It's not easy to describe since this happened so long ago, but the walls were breathing, the floors were moving, people looked nearly unrecognizable, and it was a very intense experience. I also felt like I was overheating, likely from biking around for a while then sitting in a non-air conditioned room with 8 other people. I went and sat next to the window, attempting to cool down and to escape the second hand cigarette smoke that felt like poison every time I inhaled a whiff of it. Soon though, I couldn't handle it anymore. There were too many people there, and I was the only one tripping. They were all staring at me and expecting me to do something funny I guess, but it was really upsetting my trip. I ended up taking a few hits out of a bong, which intensified the trip, though seemed to help with my anxiety.

Shortly after hitting the bong, I left, and rode my bike around the town a bit more, before returning home. By then, the trip was wearing off, and I had spent a lot more time at my friend's house than I thought. I remember taking a shower and smoking some more cannabis, but I don't remember anything else after that. I don't recall any nausea on this trip, but all my trips since have included a fair share of nausea, so I'm likely just forgetting things.

Overall, it was a good experience, though too intense for a first time in my opinion. I didn't take a dose that high again for years. Being in nature was definitely my favourite part of this trip, and being around people who were loud, annoying, and not tripping was the low point. Luckily, this trip never degraded far enough for me to consider it a bad trip, but it taught me just how important set and setting are when taking a psychedelic substance.
